resumo: What politics and democracy are, what the Constitution is for, and where everyone's money comes from.

glossario.simples: A way of governing in which power comes from the people, who choose their representatives by voting.
To come from.
The time an elected person stays in office. In Portuguese: mandato.
A person chosen to speak and decide on behalf of a group.
A vote in which people choose their representatives.
The highest law of the country; no other law can go against it.
Rights that help everyone live well, like education, health, housing and leisure.
Money that people and companies pay to the government to pay for services for everyone.
Proof of a purchase. It shows what was bought and how much it cost. In Portuguese: nota fiscal.
A plan that shows how much money the government expects to have and how it will spend it during the year.
When many different ideas and parties live side by side and can express themselves.
Groups of people with similar ideas who organize themselves to run in elections.

glossario.termo: Statute of the Child and Adolescent
glossario.simples: A 1990 law that brings together the rights of children and teenagers. It is also called ECA, from its name in Portuguese (Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente).
Sistema Único de Saúde (Unified Health System): free public health care all over Brazil.
Signing a student up at a school.
Something that belongs to everyone, not to just one person.
Something the law guarantees you.
Something you must do.
A written rule that applies to everyone and must be followed.
The way people decide together on rules and on how to use what belongs to everyone.

slides.titulo: Politics is how a group decides about what belongs to everyone
slides.texto: The school, the town square and the bus belong to everyone. In **politics**, we agree on the rules and on how to use everyone's money.

quadros.txt: The class is going on a field trip. Some want to go to the zoo. Others want to go to the museum.
Each person explains their idea. Then everyone votes. The idea with the most votes wins.
You also agree on classroom rules, like waiting your turn to speak.
And you choose a class **representative**, who takes everyone's requests to the principal.

slides.moral: Talking, voting, agreeing on rules and choosing someone to speak for everyone: that is already politics!

slides.titulo: Politics is in almost everything around you
slides.texto: Many things are **public**, which means they belong to everyone. They follow laws, which are rules for everyone, and they use public money.

cards.txt: The Constitution guarantees food for students at public schools.
cards.mais: The Constitution also mentions school supplies, transportation and health care for students.

cards.txt: The city organizes the bus that runs in your neighborhood.
cards.mais: For the Constitution, public transportation is an essential service, which means it cannot be missing. Inside the city, the municipality is in charge of it.

cards.txt: It gives free care through the SUS, Brazil's public health system.
cards.mais: The SUS works all over Brazil and treats anyone, free of charge.

cards.txt: Squares belong to the city, which takes care of them.
cards.mais: By law, when a new neighborhood is registered, its streets and squares become property of the municipality.

cards.txt: Paving, streetlights and garbage collection are paid for with public money.
cards.mais: The mayor has a team of secretaries, who head the city departments. Each one takes care of an area, like cleaning, lighting or transportation.

slides.titulo: In Brazil, power comes from the people
slides.texto: The Constitution says: “All power emanates from the people”. To emanate means to come from. This is called **democracy**.

itens.txt: In elections, each person votes in secret. Every vote counts the same.
Whoever wins becomes a representative and decides on behalf of everyone.
The time in office is the **term of office**. For most offices, it lasts 4 years.
In the next election, the people choose again and can replace whoever is there.

slides.coruja: Getting more than 200 million people together to vote on every law is not possible. That is why we choose representatives.

slides.titulo: The Constitution is Brazil's highest law
slides.texto: It is like the country's rule book. The one in force today is from **1988**.

itens.txt: It says how the country is organized and who takes care of what.
No other law can go against it.
It applies to everyone, including the people who govern.
It guarantees **social rights**, like education, health, food, housing and leisure.
It can be changed, but that is much harder than changing an ordinary law.

slides.coruja: It got the nickname “Citizen Constitution”, because it expanded people's rights.

slides.titulo: Where does the money that pays for schools and hospitals come from?
slides.texto: A big part comes from **taxes**: money that people and companies pay to the government. There is tax even on snacks and toys.

itens.txt: The receipt shows, roughly, how much of the price was tax.
This money pays for schools, hospitals, police, roads and much more.
The **budget** is the plan that says how the money will be spent during the year.
The government prepares the budget. The people's representatives review it, can change it and vote on it.

slides.coruja: In the city, the budget is voted on by the city councilors (vereadores). In the country, by the deputies and senators.

slides.texto: A **right** is what the law guarantees you. A **duty** is what you must do.

itens: Health, food, school, leisure and respect, for all children.
Playing, giving your opinion and taking part in political life, in the ways the law allows.
Being treated equally by the law.
colunas.exemplo: Playing is a right: it is written in the Statute of the Child and Adolescent (ECA).

itens: Following the laws, including the people who govern.
Going to school from age 4 to 17. Parents must take care of the enrollment.
Voting, for most adults between 18 and 70.
colunas.exemplo: Voting is a right and a duty at the same time. Stop 7 explains elections.

slides.titulo: Politics is not just fighting on TV
slides.texto: People think differently. The Constitution protects the freedom to think and to speak.

itens.txt: You can disagree with respect: speaking, listening and exchanging ideas.
Brazil has many parties and many ideas. This is called **pluralism**.
No one can lose rights because of their political opinion.
This site shows facts, always with a source. It does not tell you who to vote for.

slides.coruja: Before you pass on a news story, check where it came from.

opcoes: Only the fights between politicians that you see on TV
The way a group decides about what belongs to everyone
A subject that only matters to adults
slides.explica: Politics is deciding as a group about what belongs to everyone: in your class, in your city and in your country. Children take part too!

slides.pergunta: Where does a big part of the money that pays for public schools come from?
opcoes: From the taxes that people and companies pay
From monthly fees paid by the students
slides.explica: Public school is free for students. It is paid for with public money, and a big part of that money comes from taxes.
